audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 17, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for assassination planning, Hushai's counterstrategy, total-war imagery, providence framing, priests and young messengers, unnamed girl's intelligence work, Bahurim woman's concealment, Ahithophel's suicide, family order, burial, military genealogy, and material support for hungry refugees.

verses.restored: Ahithophel said to Absalom, Please let me choose twelve thousand men. I will arise and pursue David tonight.

familiar.text: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:

modern.text: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אֶל אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם אֶבְחֲרָ֣ה נָּ֗א שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֨לֶף֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְאָק֛וּמָה וְאֶרְדְּפָ֥ה אַחֲרֵי דָוִ֖ד הַלָּֽיְלָה

verses.restored: I will come upon him while he is weary and weak-handed, terrify him, and all people with him will flee. I will strike king alone.

familiar.text: And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:

modern.text: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king

original.text: וְאָב֣וֹא עָלָ֗יו וְה֤וּא יָגֵ֨עַ֙ וּרְפֵ֣ה יָדַ֔יִם וְהַֽחֲרַדְתִּ֣י אֹת֔וֹ וְנָ֖ס כָּל הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֑וֹ וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְבַדּֽוֹ

verses.restored: I will return all people to you. Return of all depends on man you seek; all people will be at peace.

familiar.text: And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.

modern.text: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”

original.text: וְאָשִׁ֥יבָה כָל הָעָ֖ם אֵלֶ֑יךָ כְּשׁ֣וּב הַכֹּ֔ל הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כָּל הָעָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Word was right in eyes of Absalom and in eyes of all elders of Israel.

familiar.text: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.

modern.text: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.

original.text: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Absalom said, Please call also Hushai the Archite, and let us hear what is in his mouth as well.

familiar.text: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.

modern.text: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם קְרָ֣א נָ֔א גַּ֖ם לְחוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֑י וְנִשְׁמְעָ֥ה מַה בְּפִ֖יו גַּם הֽוּא

verses.restored: Hushai came to Absalom. Absalom spoke to him, saying, According to this word Ahithophel spoke. Shall we do his word? If not, you speak.

familiar.text: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak thou.

modern.text: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל אַבְשָׁלוֹם֒ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל הֲנַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת דְּבָר֑וֹ אִם אַ֖יִן אַתָּ֥ה דַבֵּֽר

verses.restored: Hushai said to Absalom, Counsel Ahithophel counseled is not good this time.

familiar.text: And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.

modern.text: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חוּשַׁ֖י אֶל אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא טוֹבָ֧ה הָעֵצָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר יָעַ֥ץ אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל בַּפַּ֥עַם הַזֹּֽאת

verses.restored: Hushai said, You know your father and his men, that they are mighty and bitter in soul, like bear robbed of cubs in field. Your father is a man of war and will not lodge with people.

familiar.text: For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

modern.text: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אַתָּ֣ה יָ֠דַעְתָּ אֶת אָבִ֨יךָ וְאֶת אֲנָשָׁ֜יו כִּ֧י גִבֹּרִ֣ים הֵ֗מָּה וּמָרֵ֥י נֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ הֵ֔מָּה כְּדֹ֥ב שַׁכּ֖וּל בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְאָבִ֨יךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יָלִ֖ין אֶת הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Look, now he hides in one of pits or in one place. When some fall at first, hearer will hear and say, There is a slaughter among people following Absalom.

familiar.text: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.

modern.text: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’

original.text: הִנֵּ֨ה עַתָּ֤ה הֽוּא נֶחְבָּא֙ בְּאַחַ֣ת הַפְּחָתִ֔ים א֖וֹ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַמְּקוֹמֹ֑ת וְהָיָ֗ה כִּנְפֹ֤ל בָּהֶם֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה וְשָׁמַ֤ע הַשֹּׁמֵ֨עַ֙ וְאָמַ֔ר הָֽיְתָה֙ מַגֵּפָ֔ה בָּעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֹֽם

verses.restored: Even son of strength whose heart is like heart of lion will utterly melt, because all Israel knows your father is mighty and those with him are sons of strength.

familiar.text: And he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.

modern.text: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.

original.text: וְה֣וּא גַם בֶּן חַ֗יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִבּ֛וֹ כְּלֵ֥ב הָאַרְיֵ֖ה הִמֵּ֣ס יִמָּ֑ס כִּֽי יֹדֵ֤עַ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּי גִבּ֣וֹר אָבִ֔יךָ וּבְנֵי חַ֖יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Therefore I counsel: let all Israel surely gather to you, from Dan to Beersheba, like sand by sea for multitude, and you go to battle in your person.

familiar.text: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.

modern.text: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.

original.text: כִּ֣י יָעַ֗צְתִּי הֵ֠אָסֹף יֵאָסֵ֨ף עָלֶ֤יךָ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר עַל הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וּפָנֶ֥יךָ הֹלְכִ֖ים בַּקְרָֽב

verses.restored: We will come upon him in one of places where he is found and settle upon him as dew falls upon ground. We will not leave of him and all men with him even one.

familiar.text: So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.

modern.text: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.

original.text: וּבָ֣אנוּ אֵלָ֗יו באחת הַמְּקוֹמֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצָ֣א שָׁ֔ם וְנַ֣חְנוּ עָלָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִפֹּ֥ל הַטַּ֖ל עַל הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא נ֥וֹתַר בּ֛וֹ וּבְכָל הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֖וֹ גַּם אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: If he gathers into a city, all Israel will carry ropes to that city and drag it to wadi until not even a pebble is found there.

familiar.text: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.

modern.text: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found.”

original.text: וְאִם אֶל עִיר֙ יֵֽאָסֵ֔ף וְהִשִּׂ֧יאוּ כָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל הָעִ֥יר הַהִ֖יא חֲבָלִ֑ים וְסָחַ֤בְנוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד הַנַּ֔חַל עַ֛ד אֲשֶֽׁר לֹא נִמְצָ֥א שָׁ֖ם גַּם צְרֽוֹר

verses.restored: Absalom and all men of Israel said, Counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than counsel of Ahithophel. YHWH had commanded to frustrate good counsel of Ahithophel so YHWH might bring evil upon Absalom.

familiar.text: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.

modern.text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom. Hushai’s Warning Saves David (Psalms 55:1–23)

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וְכָל אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל טוֹבָ֗ה עֲצַת֙ חוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֔י מֵעֲצַ֖ת אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל וַיהוָ֣ה צִוָּ֗ה לְהָפֵ֞ר אֶת עֲצַ֤ת אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה לְבַעֲב֗וּר הָבִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶל אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶת הָרָעָֽה

verses.restored: Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus Ahithophel counseled Absalom and elders of Israel, and thus and thus I counseled.

familiar.text: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.

modern.text: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אֶל צָד֤וֹק וְאֶל אֶבְיָתָר֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים כָּזֹ֣את וְכָזֹ֗את יָעַ֤ץ אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל֙ אֶת אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָזֹ֥את וְכָזֹ֖את יָעַ֥צְתִּי אָֽנִי

verses.restored: Now send quickly and tell David, saying, Do not lodge tonight at crossings of wilderness. Crossing, cross over, lest king and all people with him be swallowed.

familiar.text: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.

modern.text: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה שִׁלְח֣וּ מְהֵרָה֩ וְהַגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר אַל תָּ֤לֶן הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְגַ֖ם עָב֣וֹר תַּעֲב֑וֹר פֶּ֚ן יְבֻלַּ֣ע לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel because they could not be seen entering city. A young woman/servant girl went and told them, and they went and told king David.

familiar.text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by Enrogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.

modern.text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.

original.text: וִיהוֹנָתָ֨ן וַאֲחִימַ֜עַץ עֹמְדִ֣ים בְּעֵין רֹגֵ֗ל וְהָלְכָ֤ה הַשִּׁפְחָה֙ וְהִגִּ֣ידָה לָהֶ֔ם וְהֵם֙ יֵֽלְכ֔וּ וְהִגִּ֖ידוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֛וּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת לָב֥וֹא הָעִֽירָה

verses.restored: A young man saw them and told Absalom. They both went quickly and came to house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in courtyard. They went down into it.

familiar.text: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.

modern.text: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.

original.text: וַיַּ֤רְא אֹתָם֙ נַ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ שְׁנֵיהֶ֨ם מְהֵרָ֜ה וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל בֵּֽית אִ֣ישׁ בְּבַחוּרִ֗ים וְל֥וֹ בְאֵ֛ר בַּחֲצֵר֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥רְדוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Woman took covering and spread it over mouth of well, and spread crushed grain upon it, so thing was not known.

familiar.text: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.

modern.text: Then the man’s wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, scattering grain over it so nobody would know a thing.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אֶת הַמָּסָךְ֙ עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַתִּשְׁטַ֥ח עָלָ֖יו הָֽרִפ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: Servants of Absalom came to woman at house and said, Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? Woman said to them, They crossed over brook of water. They sought and did not find, and returned to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And when Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

modern.text: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַבְדֵי֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶֽל הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבַּ֗יְתָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֗ה אֲחִימַ֨עַץ֙ וִיה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה עָבְר֖וּ מִיכַ֣ל הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֔אוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: After they went, messengers came up from well, went, and told king David. They said to David, Arise and quickly cross water, because thus Ahithophel counseled against you.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.

modern.text: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י אַחֲרֵ֣י לֶכְתָּ֗ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ מֵֽהַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל דָּוִ֗ד ק֣וּמוּ וְעִבְר֤וּ מְהֵרָה֙ אֶת הַמַּ֔יִם כִּי כָ֛כָה יָעַ֥ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל

verses.restored: David arose and all people with him, and they crossed Jordan. By light of morning not one was missing who had not crossed Jordan.

familiar.text: Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.

modern.text: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.

modern.text: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.

translation_notes: Ahithophel's plan is targeted assassination designed to exploit exhaustion and separate a leader from followers. Hushai counters it with an even larger total-war fantasy to delay action.
Hushai's counsel is strategically deceptive. Its imagery includes annihilating every follower and destroying a sheltering city; delay does not make the proposal ethically humane.
Verse 14 calls Ahithophel's counsel 'good' tactically while framing its defeat as Divine purpose. Tactical effectiveness and moral goodness must not be confused.
Priests, their sons, an unnamed girl, a young observer, and a Bahurim woman become an intelligence network. The unnamed women perform decisive and dangerous work.
The woman lies to armed searchers to protect people hidden in her well. Protective deception under lethal threat is ethically distinct from exploitative dishonesty.

Ahithophel dies by suicide after arranging his household. The text reports planning and death without giving his inner state; it must never be romanticized as honor, control, wisdom, or an appropriate response to humiliation.
Amasa's genealogy varies across witnesses, including Israelite/Ishmaelite. Ethnic variants must not become contempt.
The chapter ends not with strategy but with food, beds, vessels, and care for hungry, exhausted, thirsty people. Material support sustains survival.
safety_note: Maximum suicide-misuse safeguards: Do not praise or imitate Ahithophel's death, present suicide as dignified response to rejection, or assume motives not stated. In real life, suicidal crisis calls for immediate human contact, safety, and professional support. Also protect the unnamed women and young messengers from being romanticized as expendable intelligence assets.
